step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram features an internal employee user authenticating via OpenID, passing traffic through an ELB to an ECS cluster, which coordinates authorization via an authentication Lambda function. The ECS container interacts with a business logic Lambda function (connecting to DynamoDB) and an S3 bucket for file attachments.

graph.name: GE Avio Special Expense Management System
graph.notes: System processes expense ticket submissions and approvals, separating metadata into DynamoDB and documents into encrypted S3 storage.

nodes.name: Employee / User
nodes.notes: Initiates authentication and accesses the web application.

nodes.name: OpenID Provider
nodes.notes: Corporate identity provider for OpenID authentication.

nodes.name: Elastic Load Balancer
nodes.notes: Routes authentication requests to container service.

nodes.name: Amazon ECS
nodes.notes: Hosts application front-end container and API Gateway container.

nodes.name: Amazon S3
nodes.notes: Stores financial document attachments encrypted with KMS.

edges.notes: ECS delegates authorization check to Lambda.
ECS delivers single-page application to user.
User application interacts with ECS API Gateway container.
Lambda reads and writes ticket metadata to DynamoDB.
Document attachments stored into S3 bucket.
